biography: Marçal Müller, a name whispered with a mix of respect and trepidation in the Porsche paddock, hails from the vibrant, chaotic streets of São Paulo, Brazil. Unlike many of his peers who grew up karting in meticulously maintained circuits, Marçal cut his teeth navigating the city's treacherous backroads on a beat-up scooter, dodging stray dogs and errant taxi drivers. This baptism by fire instilled in him a fearlessness and improvisational skill that sets him apart on the track. His formal racing career began almost by accident when, at 19, he stumbled upon a local amateur race and, with borrowed equipment and raw talent, beat seasoned veterans. This raw talent got him noticed by AJR, who gave him his first seat in a Porsche. Now, at 33, Marçal finds himself at what many believe is the peak of his abilities, a seasoned competitor with a burning desire to prove himself against the very best.
drivingStyle: Marçal's driving style is a study in controlled aggression. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers, often pushing the limits of adhesion to gain an advantage. While some might call him reckless, Marçal's approach is calculated; he understands the delicate balance between risk and reward. Tire management isn't always his strongest suit, often favoring a short burst of blistering pace over a more conservative strategy. Under pressure, Marçal thrives, transforming into an even more formidable opponent, his focus sharpening as the stakes rise.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. If you don't have the heart, you'll never win."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2022 with the Porsche team, a hard-fought victory secured after a dramatic late-race overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2020 Daytona 24 Hours due to a mechanical failure, costing AJR Racing a likely victory.
